goal.summary: Make the dependency-audit CI gate resilient to transient npm registry timeouts without weakening vulnerability detection or reporting false green.
constraints: Keep registry-unavailable failures blocking unless an explicitly approved evidence-preserving policy exists
Preserve pnpm lockfile and frozen install behavior
Use no real credentials or production data
Keep the existing stable CI job names
exclusions: replacing audit with an unapproved weaker scanner
dependency upgrades unrelated to the timeout

Transient audit timeouts receive bounded retries or an approved equivalent and produce actionable redacted diagnostics.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: The audit command currently uses pnpm audit --audit-level=high and its registry retries can consume several minutes before failing.
The adapter job depends on successful default gates and must not run or pass when audit evidence is unavailable.

design.summary: First establish the repository-approved resilience policy, then implement one bounded audit execution seam with preserved exit semantics and diagnostics, then verify the full workflow.
candidateApproaches: bounded retry/backoff around the existing pnpm audit
approved alternate advisory retrieval with equivalent high-severity semantics
fail-fast diagnostics only if retries are not safe
design.selectionRule: Choose the smallest approach that preserves audit coverage and fail-closed behavior; reject any approach that reports success without current advisory evidence.
design.failurePolicy: Vulnerability findings and unavailable/ambiguous advisory evidence remain nonzero failures.
